title: Class templates
recap: A class template describes a family of types, not just a family of functions. Pair<int> and Pair<double> are different types with correspondingly typed members.
Use the template parameter for the stored data, not just for a function's return type. Hard-coding int members would lose fractional values before pairSum could preserve them.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Complete the Pair<T> struct with two value-initialized members, T first{} and T second{}, then implement pairSum(pair), returning their sum as T. The member declarations are intentionally left for you. Support Pair<int> and Pair<double>; template arguments choose the member types as well as the function instance.
hints: Add both members inside Pair, using T rather than int.
Return the sum without converting through a fixed numeric type.
